definition: a move in chess that puts the opponent's king in an inescapable position, ending the game
hook: Checkmate isn't really about a mate at all.
modernAnchor: We shout it in arguments and boardrooms long after the chessboard's gone. Checkmate. Case closed.
journey: Chess traveled from India to Persia, where players called the winning move shah mat.
Shah meant king. Mat meant helpless, trapped, unable to escape, not dead as many assume today.
Arabic traders carried the game and its phrase into Europe, where shah mat slowly became checkmate.
English speakers heard mate and assumed a companion, not a king with nowhere left to run.
